open_points.subject: NodeExecution ownership for operation elements
open_points.text: "Their shape, which events write one, and their order are `runs`' (A15). The record that concludes an operation element is written by `effects` inside its outcome call (A11 rule 1), in the shape `runs` defines" and "`effects` owns A10 and A11: ... the in-flight record, the send, the outcome record"
open_points.question: Which module is the single owner of constructing the operation element's NodeExecution status/failure fields from send outcomes: `runs` or `effects`?
options: `runs` defines and builds NodeExecution records; `effects` returns normalized send outcomes
`effects` builds the NodeExecution record and `runs` only owns non-operation records
`store` enforces a canonical NodeExecution write shape independent of caller
open_points.default_guess: `effects` builds operation NodeExecution records, while `runs` owns ordering/lifecycle constraints.

open_points.subject: Disclosure-class assignment when values are produced
open_points.text: "`runs` ... owns ... the run-time class of a value (A07 rule 3)" and "then one store call writes the outcome: ... the values it produced" (`effects`) and `functions` owns trial/admission flows that also write TrialExecution outputs as StoredValues
open_points.question: Who computes and sets `disclosure_class` on produced StoredValues/SpooledFiles for (a) operation outputs and (b) trial executions, given production happens in `effects`/`functions` but ownership is assigned to `runs`?
options: `runs` computes classes for all produced values via a shared write path
`store` derives classes from referenced inputs/ports at write time
open_points.default_guess: Producer modules compute classes with `canonical_values`, because they own the immediate execution context.

open_points.subject: Grant/revoke active-version check across same-layer modules
open_points.text: "A module may know only modules on lower lines; ... modules on one line do not know each other." with `flows, effects` on one line; and A10 rule 5 requires "A grant is given only for a node of the flow's active version"
open_points.question: How does `effects` validate "node of the flow's active version" for grant/revoke without knowing `flows` or duplicating flows-owned activation semantics?
options: `effects` reads FlowActivation and flow structure directly via `store`
`surface`/caller checks active-version eligibility through `flows` before calling `effects`
Introduce a lower-layer read capability for active-version/node validation consumed by both
open_points.default_guess: `effects` queries `store` directly for active-version and node membership.

open_points.subject: Attempt number consistency across two store calls
open_points.text: A11 flow in State 3 says "one store call writes the EffectAttempt `in_flight` ... then one store call writes the outcome: the EffectAttempt's conclusion, the next NodeExecution" while State 3 also says "`attempt_number` is computed by `store` inside the transaction that writes the record ... so no module counts on its own"
open_points.question: What is the exact ownership/mechanism that guarantees the same `attempt_number` is used for the in-flight EffectAttempt and its concluding NodeExecution across two transactions?
options: First call reserves/persists the attempt number; second call must reuse it
Second call derives number by looking up the in-flight attempt written by first call
`effects` computes/passes the number despite the "store computes" statement
open_points.default_guess: First call persists the attempt number on EffectAttempt; second call reuses that persisted number.
